data.narrative: Propose Allocate Substitute for human decision: the certificate shows 120 each (ev-cert-qty) while receiving posted 80 each (ev-recv-qty) for the held alloy, leaving a 40-each discrepancy unresolved and the original lot unavailable. Two jobs need 70 units in total, and verified substitute stock is 100 each (ev-sub-stock), enough to cover all 70 units. This option finishes in 35 hours at $3,115 incremental cost, comprising $2,975 labor and a $140 material premium on the preferred cell. Counterfactuals: Waiting for Replenishment costs $0 but finishes in 83 hours after a 48-hour lead time plus 35 production hours, well beyond the 36- and 48-hour job dues; Splitting Capacity finishes fastest in 17.5 hours but costs $3,202.50, $87.50 more than allocating the substitute. Assumptions: quantities use the current certificate, receiving and stock records; cell costs use the hourly rates provided; and substitute allocation uses only verified available stock. The held lot remains on hold and no supplier messaging is included.
